#Metadata check
```{r}
input_files <- list.files(
  pipeline_output_path,
  pattern = "^test_chem_well.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

check_results <- map_dfr(input_files, function(path) {
  # just read the header, no need to load full file
  header <- names(read_csv(path, n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE))
  first4 <- header[1:4]

  tibble(
    file = basename(path),
    col1 = first4[1],
    col2 = first4[2],
    col3 = first4[3],
    col4 = first4[4],
    all_metadata = all(str_starts(first4, "Metadata_")),
    matches_expected = setequal(
      first4,
      c("Metadata_Chemical", "Metadata_Concentration", "Metadata_Well", "Metadata_Plate")
    )
  )
})

print(check_results)

# Flag any problem files
problems <- check_results %>% filter(!matches_expected)
if (nrow(problems) > 0) {
  warning("These files do NOT have the expected 4 Metadata_ columns first:\n",
          paste(problems$file, collapse = "\n"))
} else {
  message("All files check out: first 4 columns are the expected Metadata_ columns.")
}

```
#Filter for common features for catagorical analysis
```{r}

#after simplification there are fewer features maybe stop simplifictaion
# List of replicate folders
rep_dirs <- c(
  rep1 = "../Output/rep1",
  rep2 = "../Output/rep2",
  rep3 = "../Output/rep3"
)

# File paths
rep_files <- file.path(
  rep_dirs,
  "test_chem_well_pearson_0.9.csv"
)
names(rep_files) <- names(rep_dirs)


# Read each file
rep_data <- imap(rep_files, function(path, rep_name) {
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
})


# Get feature names
retained_features <- map(rep_data, names)


# Intersection of feature names across all three reps
common_features <- reduce(retained_features, intersect)

length(common_features)


# Keep only the common features
rep_common <- imap(rep_data, function(df, rep_name) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::select(all_of(common_features))
})


# Write common-feature files
iwalk(rep_common, function(df, rep_name) {
  write_csv(
    df,
    file.path(
      rep_dirs[[rep_name]],
      "test_chem_well_pearson_0.9_common.csv"
    )
  )
})
```
#Simplify features for catagorical analysis
```{r}
# Reformat one test_chem_well-style data frame: collapse verbose CellProfiler
# feature names into simplified category names and set Chemical_Conc_Well_Plate
# as the row name. Wrapped as a function so it can be applied to every
# feature-selected variant produced by the previous notebook.
reformat_feature_names <- function(test_chem_well) {

test_chem_well <- as.data.frame(test_chem_well)
variances <- apply(test_chem_well, 2, var)
variances[1:4] <- 1

test_chem_well <- test_chem_well[, variances != 0 & !is.na(variances)]

feature_cols  <- test_chem_well[, 5:ncol(test_chem_well)]

features <- data.frame(feature = colnames(test_chem_well[-c(1:4)])) %>%
   mutate(
     feature_base = str_remove(feature, "_(cells|cytoplasm|nuclei)$"),
    module = str_extract(feature, "^[^_]+"),
    region = str_extract(feature, "(cells|cytoplasm|nuclei)$"),
    channel1 = case_when(
      module == "Correlation" ~
        str_match(feature,
          "^Correlation_[^_]+_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_"
        )[, 2],
      TRUE ~ str_extract(feature, "_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)(_|$)") %>%
               str_remove_all("_")
    ),
    channel2 = case_when(
      module == "Correlation" ~
        str_match(feature,
          "^Correlation_[^_]+_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_(AGP|ER|DNA|Mito|RNA)_"
        )[, 3],
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(module, region, channel1, channel2), as.character))

features <- features %>%
  group_by(region, channel1, channel2, module) %>%
  mutate(cat_group = cur_group_id()) %>%
  mutate(ft_no = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

ft_colnames <- features %>%
  dplyr::select(region, channel1, channel2, module, cat_group, ft_no)

#Concatenate region, channel, and module
ft_colnames2 <- apply(
  ft_colnames[, c("region", "channel1", "channel2", "module")],
  1,
  \(x) paste(na.omit(x), collapse = "_")
)
ft_colnames2 <- as.data.frame(ft_colnames2)
colnames(ft_colnames2) <- "features"

sample_info <- as.data.frame(colnames(test_chem_well[c(1:4)]))
colnames(sample_info) <- "features"
colnames(ft_colnames2) <- "features"

fts <- rbind(sample_info, ft_colnames2)

#Replace the original features names with the reformatted feature names
colnames(test_chem_well) <- t(fts) # run code up to here for BMDExpress formatting

##Concatenate chemical name, plate number, and well ID in one column
test_chem_well$Chemical <- paste0(test_chem_well$Metadata_Chemical, "_",test_chem_well$Metadata_Concentration, "_", test_chem_well$Metadata_Well, "_",test_chem_well$Metadata_Plate)

test_chem_well <- test_chem_well[, !names(test_chem_well) %in% c("Metadata_Plate", "Metadata_Well","Metadata_Concentration", "Metadata_Chemical")]

##make chemicals info the row name
rows <- test_chem_well$Chemical

rownames(test_chem_well) <- rows

test_chem_well <- test_chem_well %>%
  dplyr::select(-Chemical)

test_chem_well
list(
  data = test_chem_well,
  ft_colnames2 = ft_colnames2
)
}

# Loop over every feature-selected variant saved by the previous notebook
# (test_chem_well.csv, test_chem_well_lowvariance.csv,
#  test_chem_well_pearson_*.csv, test_chem_well_lowvar_pearson_*.csv, ...)
# and write out a correspondingly-named, reformatted CSV.
input_files <- list.files(
  pipeline_output_path,
  pattern = "^test_chem_well.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

walk(input_files, function(path) {
  message("Reformatting: ", basename(path))

  df <- read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  result <- reformat_feature_names(df)

  reformatted <- result$data
  ft_colnames2 <- result$ft_colnames2

  out_name <- str_replace(
    basename(path),
    "^test_chem_well",
    "test_chem_cat"
  )

  write.csv(
    reformatted,
    file.path(
      pipeline_output_path,
      "feature_results",
      out_name
    ),
    row.names = TRUE
  )

  # Save category labels for this feature set
  write.csv(
    ft_colnames2,
    file.path(
      pipeline_output_path,
      "feature_results",
      str_replace(
        out_name,
        "\\.csv$",
        "_ft_colnames2.csv"
      )
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
})
```
